en.title: D. E. Shaw OA #1: Sorted After Removing a Subarray
en.description: Given an integer array arr of length n, count the subarrays (contiguous segments, distinguished by position) whose removal leaves an array that is non-empty and sorted in non-decreasing order (adjacent elements may be equal).
en.input: The first line contains an integer n; the second line contains n integers arr[0..n−1]. 1≤n≤200000, 1≤arr[i]≤10^9.
en.output: Output one integer: the number of subarrays that satisfy the condition.
en.explanation:
Example 1: arr=[1,2,1,2] has 10 subarrays. The 7 removals that leave [1,2], [2], [1,1,2], [1,2], [1], [1,2,2], and [1,2] satisfy the condition; removing [1] leaves [2,1,2] and removing the last [2] leaves [1,2,1], neither of which is sorted, and removing the whole array leaves an empty array, which also fails.
Example 2: removing [3], [3,1], or [1,2] satisfies the condition, so the answer is 3.
Example 3: the qualifying subarrays are [1,2,2,6], [1,2,2,6,1], [2,2,6], [2,2,6,1], [2,2,6,1,3], [2,6,1], [2,6,1,3], [6,1], [6,1,3], and [1,3], so the answer is 10.
hints: The remaining array is a prefix joined with a suffix.
Both the prefix and the suffix must be non-decreasing, and at the junction the left element must not exceed the right one.
Since the suffix is sorted, you can binary search for the first position it can be joined at.
